hero.headline: Paris St-Germain wins second consecutive Champions League title in penalty shootout over Arsenal
hero.body:
Paris St-Germain retained the Champions League title by defeating Arsenal in a penalty shootout at the Puskas Arena in Budapest. The match ended with Gabriel Magalhães missing the decisive spot-kick, handing PSG their second straight European crown.

The final was tightly contested throughout. Kai Havertz gave Arsenal an early lead with a well-struck finish into the top corner after collecting a loose ball from a Marquinhos clearance. PSG responded through Ousmane Dembélé, who converted from the penalty spot in the 65th minute after Cristhian Mosquera's clumsy challenge on Khvicha Kvaratskhelia.

Arsenal's manager Mikel Arteta set his team up defensively, prioritizing solidity and compression of spaces. The approach proved effective in the opening stages, with PSG struggling to create clear opportunities despite dominating possession. Arsenal's back line, led by Gabriel, made crucial tackles and blocks to keep PSG at arm's length.

When the deadlock could not be broken through regulation and extra time, the match went to penalties. Eberechi Eze missed for Arsenal in the second round after a stuttering run, though David Raya kept his side alive by denying Nuno Mendes in the third round.

Gabriel stepped up for the decisive kick knowing he had to score to keep Arsenal's hopes alive. He was briefly delayed by referee Daniel Siebert as nerves mounted. The defender opted for power but blazed his attempt over the crossbar, sparking celebrations from the PSG fans behind the goal as red flares lit up the stadium.

The defeat marks a painful conclusion to what had otherwise been a historic season for Arsenal. The club won their first Premier League title in 22 years earlier in May, ending a drought that began after their Invincibles campaign in 2004. An open bus parade to celebrate the domestic triumph was scheduled for the following day, creating a bittersweet end to their campaign.

For PSG, the victory confirms their status as Europe's dominant force. Becoming back-to-back Champions League winners underscores their position among the continent's elite clubs.

The final was shaped by contrasting approaches, with Arsenal defending aggressively while PSG sought to impose their attacking patterns. Arsenal's young midfielder Myles Lewis-Skelly impressed throughout, while Gabriel proved to be a commanding presence at the back before his penalty heartbreak.

The shootout loss denied Arsenal the chance to complete a domestic and European double, a feat that would have cemented their status among the greatest modern teams. Instead, they must reflect on narrowly falling short in the competition's showpiece event.

cards.headline: U.S. military disables ship attempting to breach Iranian port blockade
cards.body:
The U.S. military prevented another vessel from reaching an Iranian port on Friday, continuing its enforcement of a naval blockade in the Strait of Hormuz. U.S. Central Command announced the action against a ship flying under a Gambian flag after it ignored repeated warnings from American forces.

The disabled vessel represents another instance of the military taking direct action as part of the broader blockade that has closed Iranian ports to commercial shipping. Central Command did not provide specific details about how the ship was disabled, the condition of the vessel, or the status of its crew.

The Strait of Hormuz, a narrow waterway between Iran and the Arabian Peninsula, represents a critical route for global oil shipments. The U.S. blockade has created significant shipping disruptions in recent weeks by preventing vessels from entering Iranian ports.

This enforcement action comes as Washington and Tehran work toward a potential agreement that could reopen the Strait of Hormuz and extend a current ceasefire. Diplomatic sources have indicated that reopening the strait constitutes a key element of any deal between the two governments. That agreement was announced this week and now awaits approval from President Trump and Iranian officials.

The timing of the military intervention adds complexity to ongoing negotiations between the two nations. The blockade and related diplomatic efforts follow months of escalating tensions between the United States and Iran over regional security and economic matters.

Central Command has not disclosed the total number of vessels that have encountered the blockade. This marks at least the second publicly known instance of direct military action against a ship attempting to breach the blockade, though the military has not revealed how many ships complied with warnings and turned away before facing intervention.

The blockade represents part of a broader U.S. strategy to apply pressure on Iran while simultaneously pursuing diplomatic talks. The delicate balance between military enforcement and negotiation efforts highlights the complexity of the current situation in the region.

U.S. officials have characterized the blockade as necessary for regional security and to support negotiations. However, the enforcement action demonstrates the military dimension of American policy toward Iran, even as diplomats work to reach a settlement.

The outcome of the negotiations could significantly reshape the strategic landscape in the Middle East. If successful, the agreement would remove restrictions on Iranian shipping and represent a major shift in U.S. policy toward Tehran.

The incident also reflects broader maritime tensions in the region, where multiple actors maintain competing interests and capabilities. The Strait of Hormuz has long served as a flashpoint for geopolitical competition, and the current blockade underscores its continued strategic importance.

cards.headline: Ebola outbreak in DR Congo kills over 245 as health agencies warn of rapid spread
cards.body:
An Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has resulted in 65 confirmed deaths, with 246 suspected cases reported so far in Ituri province. Health officials and international organizations are expressing deep concern about the speed at which the virus is spreading.

The outbreak is concentrated mainly in the Mongwalu and Rwampara health zones, with suspected cases also appearing in the neighboring city of Bunia. Ituri province, which borders Uganda and South Sudan, has presented particular challenges for disease control efforts. The region is home to mining towns where significant population movement occurs regularly, making it difficult for health workers to track and contain cases.

Uganda has confirmed its own Ebola outbreak, with a 59-year-old man dying in a Kampala hospital after traveling from the DRC. This cross-border spread has prompted urgent international coordination efforts.

A concerning aspect of this outbreak is the specific strain involved. The Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention confirmed that the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola has been detected in samples from the affected areas. Unlike the more common Zaire strain, for which vaccines exist, there is currently no licensed vaccine for Bundibugyo. Only two previous outbreaks of this strain have been documented, in 2007 and 2012.

The World Health Organization has estimated the death rate at between 30 percent and 50 percent based on confirmed cases. WHO officials have called for cooperation among neighboring countries and international partners to prevent further spread. The organization's director general emphasized the importance of rapid regional coordination given the high movement of people between affected areas and neighboring countries.

The Africa CDC has convened an urgent meeting with authorities from the DRC, Uganda, and South Sudan, along with the World Health Organization and pharmaceutical companies, to coordinate response efforts.

Health workers in the region face significant obstacles. The DRC's medical infrastructure has limited resources to respond to the growing number of cases. International aid organizations, including Médecins Sans Frontières, have mobilized resources to support local health teams with equipment and expertise.

Experts point to several factors that make Ebola outbreaks common in the DRC. Close human contact with animal reservoirs, likely bats or primates, combined with population movement between rural and urban areas, creates conditions favorable for the virus's spread. The tropical climate and high rainforest coverage also contribute to these regular outbreaks.

The DRC has experienced 16 Ebola outbreaks since the virus was first identified there in 1976, making it crucial for health authorities to work quickly to contain this latest outbreak before it expands further into neighboring communities.

cards.headline: New car sales decline for eighth consecutive month
cards.teaser: About one million buyers have disappeared from the new car market as sales continue falling.
cards.body:
New car sales in the United States have dropped for the eighth straight month, with approximately one million buyers no longer purchasing new vehicles. The sustained decline reflects ongoing pressure on consumers as vehicle affordability becomes increasingly difficult.

Demand for electric vehicles has collapsed as part of the broader sales downturn. Auto manufacturers have maintained profitability despite the stagnating sales figures, according to industry reports. Drivers continue to face financial constraints that make new car purchases unaffordable for a growing segment of the population.

cards.headline: Judge orders review of Trump's $1.8 billion fund in IRS case
cards.teaser: A federal judge has reopened examination of whether a settlement creating Trump's anti-weaponization fund constitutes fraud.
cards.body:
A federal judge in Miami has reopened President Trump's $10 billion lawsuit against the IRS following a third-party motion challenging the legitimacy of a settlement agreement. The motion alleges that the $1.8 billion "anti-weaponization" fund created through the settlement is "a product of collusion and is itself a fraud on the court."

The lawsuit was originally filed by Trump and his sons after their personal and business tax returns were leaked by a former IRS contractor. Since the fund's announcement earlier this month, it has generated significant backlash and exposed divisions within the Republican Party over its creation and purpose.

cards.headline: Trump administration clarifies green card policy after confusion over residency requirements
cards.teaser: The Department of Homeland Security said most immigrants will not need to leave the United States to obtain green cards despite earlier policy messaging.
cards.body:
The Trump administration sought to clarify green card policy changes after initial messaging created confusion and anxiety among immigrants. The Department of Homeland Security stated that most immigrants would not be required to leave the country to receive green cards, contradicting earlier interpretations of the policy.

The new green card rules sparked fear among those seeking permanent residency status. Immigrants and advocacy groups reported uncertainty about the path to legal residency following the administration's initial announcements. The policy changes represent a significant shift in legal immigration procedures, though officials now say the impact may be more limited than originally understood.

cards.headline: New Jersey governor and DHS secretary coordinate response to protests at immigration facility
cards.teaser: Governor Mikie Sherrill deployed state police to a Newark immigration detention center facing escalating protests.
cards.body:
Protests outside the Delaney Hall immigration detention center in Newark, New Jersey continued into their ninth day on Saturday, with detainees engaged in a hunger and labor strike demanding improved conditions and medical care.

State police deployed barricades to separate demonstrators supporting the detained immigrants from a group of Trump-supporting counterprotesters who gathered outside the facility. The competing groups faced off across the police barriers, with both sides chanting slogans and displaying signs reflecting their opposing positions on immigration enforcement.

cards.headline: Four men rescued from flooded cave in Laos after more than a week trapped
cards.teaser: Rescue teams freed four men from a flooded cave in Laos where they had been trapped for more than 10 days.
cards.body:
Four more miners have been freed from a flooded cave system in Laos, where they had been trapped for 10 days. This rescue followed the extraction of one miner on Friday, bringing the total number of successful rescues to five from a group of seven men who entered the cave on May 20 in search of gold.

Two miners remain missing as rescue teams continue their hazardous operation. Divers are navigating narrow, waterlogged tunnels filled with sharp rocks and collapse hazards to reach them. Rescue efforts have involved draining water from the cave system to improve conditions for the search.

cards.headline: Drone crashes into apartment building in eastern Romania
cards.teaser: A drone struck an apartment building in eastern Romania, bringing the war in neighboring Ukraine into residential areas.
cards.body:
A drone crashed into an apartment building in eastern Romania, causing a fire and panic among residents. The incident occurred in a city in the eastern part of the country, near the border with Ukraine.

Residents of the affected building described hearing a big bang before the fire started. People have only recently begun returning to check on their homes in the damaged block. The crash served as a reminder to Romanians that the ongoing war between Russia and Ukraine poses risks to neighboring countries.

cards.headline: Ecuadorian president offers to cancel tariffs after contact with Colombian candidate
cards.teaser: Ecuador is accused of interfering in Colombia's election after its leader pledged tariff relief following talks with a right-wing candidate.
cards.body:
Ecuadorian President Daniel Noboa offered to cancel tariffs after speaking with a right-wing Colombian presidential candidate ahead of the country's election. The move has prompted accusations that Ecuador is meddling in Colombia's democratic process.

Colombia holds its presidential election, with voters choosing between candidates representing different political directions. The election is viewed as an important test for the political left in Latin America, with a leftist candidate leading in polls but facing a challenge from a far-right outsider who calls himself The Tiger.

cards.headline: Australian farmers battle severe mouse plague destroying crops
cards.teaser: Farmers in Australia are dealing with a mouse infestation of thousands per hectare that is destroying crops and invading homes.
cards.body:
Australian farmers report fighting a severe mouse plague affecting agricultural regions. Farmers have documented thousands of mice per hectare across affected areas, with the rodents destroying crops and entering residential properties.

One farmer described the situation as like a decaying body, referring to the scale and impact of the infestation. The plague is causing significant agricultural damage as mice consume and contaminate grain stores and damage growing crops in the fields.

cards.headline: Iranian soccer team practices in Turkey while awaiting US visas for World Cup
cards.teaser: Iran's national soccer team is training in Turkey and preparing backup plans as they wait for visas to enter the United States.
cards.body:
The Iranian national soccer team is practicing in Turkey while still waiting for visas to enter the United States for the World Cup. The players are in limbo as the tournament approaches, with ongoing war affecting their preparations.

Team officials are developing backup plans in case the visa issues are not resolved in time. The situation has left the Iranian players uncertain about their ability to participate in the tournament on American soil.

cards.headline: Film editor Marcia Lucas dies at 80
cards.teaser: Oscar-winning editor Marcia Lucas, recognized as a creative force behind the original Star Wars trilogy, has died.
cards.body:
Marcia Lucas, the Oscar-winning film editor behind the original Star Wars trilogy, has died at age 80. She was recognized as a pivotal creative force in shaping the final versions of the films that became cultural landmarks.

Lucas, the ex-wife of director George Lucas, received an Academy Award for her editorial contributions to the Star Wars films.

hero.headline: Bus driver charged after crash kills family of four and fifth person on Virginia highway
hero.body:
A bus driver has been charged with involuntary manslaughter following a collision on Interstate 95 in Stafford County, Virginia that killed five people, including a family of four from Massachusetts who were traveling to a wedding.

The crash involved the bus striking multiple vehicles on the interstate. Among those killed were the four members of a Massachusetts family making the trip south for a wedding celebration. A fifth person also died in the collision.

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy noted that the bus driver does not speak English, though authorities have not provided additional details about how this factor may have contributed to the incident.

Involuntary manslaughter charges typically apply when someone causes death through criminal negligence or reckless conduct without intent to kill. The charges against the bus driver represent a significant development in the case as investigators continue examining the circumstances that led to the multi-vehicle collision.

The crash occurred in Stafford County, which lies between Washington D.C. and Richmond. Authorities have not released specific information about the sequence of events leading to the collision or whether other factors played a role in the crash.

The loss of the four family members in a single incident has marked a significant tragedy for their community. Officials identified the victims as a family from Massachusetts, though complete details about the fifth victim killed in the crash have not been fully disclosed in available reports.

The Washington Post reported on the charges being brought against the driver in connection with the fatal collision. As investigations continue, authorities are working to determine the exact cause of the crash and whether any contributing factors beyond the driver's actions may have played a role in the incident.

cards.headline: Judge orders review of Trump's $1.8 billion fund in IRS case
cards.teaser: A federal judge has reopened examination of whether a settlement creating Trump's anti-weaponization fund constitutes fraud.
cards.body:
A federal judge in Miami has reopened President Trump's $10 billion lawsuit against the IRS following a third-party motion challenging the legitimacy of a settlement agreement. The motion alleges that the $1.8 billion "anti-weaponization" fund created through the settlement is "a product of collusion and is itself a fraud on the court."

The lawsuit was originally filed by Trump and his sons after their personal and business tax returns were leaked by a former IRS contractor. Since the fund's announcement earlier this month, it has generated significant backlash and exposed divisions within the Republican Party over its creation and purpose.

cards.headline: Federal judge orders Trump's name removed from Kennedy Center
cards.teaser: A court ruling blocking Trump's Kennedy Center plans prompted the president to suggest the venue may never reopen.
cards.body:
A judge ordered President Trump's name scrubbed from the Kennedy Center, a decision that angered the president. Trump responded by saying the performing arts center is probably never to open again following the ruling.

Trump directed criticism at the judge's wife after the Kennedy Center decision. The ruling blocked plans Trump had for the Washington cultural institution. The case has raised questions about what happens next for the center, which now faces an uncertain future according to Trump's assessment.

cards.headline: New Jersey state police to replace federal agents at ICE facility after protests
cards.teaser: Dueling protests over detainee conditions at a New Jersey ICE detention center led to state police deployment and use of tear gas.
cards.body:
State police in New Jersey will take over security duties from federal agents at the Delaney Hall immigration detention center in Newark following clashes between opposing protest groups. Authorities deployed tear gas against protesters at the facility, and a WNBC news crew was removed from their vehicle during the confrontation.

The detention center has become a focal point for demonstrations as a hunger and labor strike inside reached its ninth day, with detainees demanding improved conditions and medical care. On Saturday, rightwing counterprotesters wearing Trump hats gathered outside to support ICE operations, while other protesters advocated for the detained immigrants. Representatives Mikie Sherrill and Markwayne Mullin worked together to address security concerns at the facility.

cards.headline: ICE agent arrested in Texas for shooting during Minnesota immigration operation
cards.teaser: An ICE agent facing charges for shooting a Venezuelan man during a Minneapolis raid has been taken into custody in Texas.
cards.body:
An ICE agent was arrested in Texas months after a shooting that occurred during an immigration enforcement operation in Minneapolis. The agent has been charged in connection with shooting a Venezuelan man during the January crackdown known as Operation Metro Surge.

The shooting happened during immigration enforcement activities in Minnesota. The agent now faces criminal charges related to the incident and was apprehended in Texas. The arrest follows the January shooting of an immigrant during the Minneapolis-area immigration operation.

cards.teaser: The Department of Homeland Security said most immigrants will not need to leave the United States to obtain green cards despite earlier policy messaging.

cards.headline: Catholic priest convicted of sexually assaulting women under his spiritual care in Texas
cards.teaser: Father Anthony Odiong was found guilty on all counts in a sexual assault trial involving women he ministered to in Texas.
cards.body:
A jury found Father Anthony Odiong guilty on all counts of sexually abusing women who were under his spiritual care. Prosecutors described faith as the weapon Odiong used against the victims during the trial in Texas.

Following the conviction, a Louisiana chapel that Odiong built removed his name from the facility. The verdict has raised questions for several Church leaders about their oversight and response. The National Catholic Reporter covered the case of the Catholic priest who was convicted of the sexual assaults in Texas.

hero.headline: SoftBank to invest up to $75 billion in French AI data centers
hero.body:
SoftBank Group announced plans to invest up to 75 billion euros, or about $52 billion, to build what would become Europe's largest artificial intelligence facility in France. The Japanese technology conglomerate will construct AI data centers as part of the major investment.

The project represents one of the largest foreign technology investments in Europe and positions France as a central hub for AI infrastructure on the continent. SoftBank's commitment to building up AI data center capacity in France comes as demand for computing power to support artificial intelligence applications continues to grow globally.

The investment will fund construction of multiple data centers dedicated to AI workloads. These facilities require significant energy and cooling infrastructure to support the intensive computational demands of training and running large AI models.

France has actively courted major technology investments in recent years, positioning itself as a favorable destination for AI research and infrastructure within Europe. The country has offered tax incentives and regulatory support to attract companies developing AI technologies.

SoftBank, led by founder and CEO Masayoshi Son, has made artificial intelligence a central focus of its investment strategy. The company has backed numerous AI startups through its Vision Fund and has increasingly directed capital toward AI infrastructure projects.

The scale of the planned investment underscores the massive capital requirements for building modern AI infrastructure. Data centers that support AI training and deployment need specialized hardware, including advanced chips, along with reliable power supplies and network connectivity.

The announcement adds to growing competition among countries and regions to establish themselves as AI technology leaders. The United States and China have dominated AI infrastructure development, but European nations have sought to build their own capabilities to avoid dependence on foreign technology providers.

Construction timelines and specific locations for the data centers were not disclosed in the initial announcement. The investment will unfold over multiple years as SoftBank develops the facilities to support AI computing workloads across Europe.

cards.headline: New car sales decline for eighth consecutive month
cards.teaser: About one million buyers have disappeared from the new car market as sales continue falling.
cards.body:
New car sales in the United States have dropped for the eighth straight month, with approximately one million buyers no longer purchasing new vehicles. The sustained decline reflects ongoing pressure on consumers as vehicle affordability becomes increasingly difficult.

Demand for electric vehicles has collapsed as part of the broader sales downturn. Auto manufacturers have maintained profitability despite the stagnating sales figures, according to industry reports. Drivers continue to face financial constraints that make new car purchases unaffordable for a growing segment of the population.

cards.headline: United Airlines flight diverted after passenger attempts to breach cockpit
cards.teaser: A 75-year-old man tried multiple times to enter the cockpit during a flight, forcing an emergency landing in Wisconsin.
cards.body:
A United Airlines flight was diverted to Madison, Wisconsin, after a passenger made multiple attempts to access the cockpit. The 75-year-old man was detained by crew members and other passengers during the flight.

The aircraft landed safely in Madison, where authorities took the passenger into custody. No criminal charges are expected to be filed against the individual.

cards.headline: China's biotechnology industry advances in drug development
cards.teaser: Clinical trials from China are drawing attention at a major oncology conference as the country's biotech sector grows.
cards.body:
Chinese clinical trials received prominent attention at an international oncology conference in Chicago, underscoring the country's growing influence in pharmaceutical research. China's expanding biotechnology capabilities have positioned it as an increasingly significant player in global drug development.

The advancement has sparked discussion about shifting competitive dynamics in the pharmaceutical sector. Observers are examining whether China's progress in biotechnology may affect traditional U.S. leadership in medical innovation and drug development.

cards.headline: Vietnamese photojournalist Dang Van Phuoc dies at 90
cards.teaser: The Associated Press photographer spent a decade documenting combat during the Vietnam War and lost his right eye to a grenade.
cards.body:
Dang Van Phuoc, a photographer for The Associated Press who covered the Vietnam War, died at age 90. The photojournalist spent ten years on the front lines of combat in his native Vietnam, documenting the conflict through his lens.

Dang lost his right eye in a grenade explosion during his wartime coverage. His work provided visual documentation of one of the most significant conflicts of the 20th century, capturing images from the battlefield throughout the long war.

cards.headline: Flight attendant retires after 66 years of service
cards.teaser: Joan Prince Crandall is ending her career as the airline industry's longest-serving flight attendant.
cards.body:
Joan Prince Crandall is retiring after working 66 years as a flight attendant, making her the longest-serving flight attendant in the airline industry. Her career spanned more than six decades in the air, beginning in 1960.

The retirement coincides with International Flight Attendant Day, which recognizes the work of cabin crew members. Crandall's exceptionally long career in aviation saw her witness dramatic changes in commercial air travel, from the early jet age through the modern era of mass air transportation.

cards.headline: Sound Transit revises light rail expansion plans in Seattle area
cards.teaser: The transit agency shelved plans for a Ballard line as it passed a revised plan for future projects.
cards.body:
The Sound Transit board approved a revised plan for its light rail expansion program, making changes to keep projects moving forward. The agency shelved a planned light rail line to the Ballard neighborhood, prompting questions from taxpayers about refunds for the canceled project.

Seattle City Council members said they would continue advocating for the Ballard light rail connection. Sound Transit cited affordability concerns in its decision to revise the original expansion plans, which were part of the agency's ST3 program approved by voters years earlier.

hero.headline: SoftBank plans up to $75 billion investment in French data centers
hero.body:
SoftBank announced plans to invest up to $75 billion in building data centers across France. The investment aims to develop and operate up to 5 gigawatts of additional data center capacity in the country.

The scale of the proposed investment would make it one of the largest infrastructure projects in France's technology sector. Data centers house the servers and computing equipment that power cloud services, artificial intelligence systems, and internet applications.

SoftBank, the Japanese conglomerate led by Masayoshi Son, has been actively investing in technology infrastructure and artificial intelligence ventures. The company previously made substantial bets on telecommunications and technology companies worldwide.

Five gigawatts of data center capacity would represent a substantial expansion of computing infrastructure in Europe. The continent has seen growing demand for data processing capabilities as companies adopt cloud computing and AI technologies.

France has been working to position itself as a technology hub within Europe, offering incentives for large technology investments. The country's government has promoted initiatives to attract data center operators and technology companies.

The timeline for the investment and construction of the data centers was not specified in the announcement. Building data center facilities typically requires several years of planning, permitting, and construction before becoming operational.

Data centers require significant electrical power to operate servers and cooling systems. The 5-gigawatt target would require substantial energy infrastructure, raising questions about power sourcing and environmental impact.

SoftBank's announcement comes as global technology companies compete to expand their computing infrastructure to support growing artificial intelligence workloads. Major cloud providers and AI companies have announced billions in data center investments across multiple countries.

The investment represents SoftBank's continued commitment to technology infrastructure despite market fluctuations in the technology sector. The company has previously invested in telecommunications networks, semiconductor design, and various technology startups through its Vision Fund.

French officials have not yet publicly commented on the proposed investment or any government support that might accompany the project.

cards.headline: Microsoft threatens legal action against security researcher over exploit disclosures
cards.teaser: Microsoft warned a security researcher of potential criminal investigation after the researcher publicly disclosed multiple zero-day vulnerabilities.
cards.body:
Microsoft warned a security researcher known as Nightmare Eclipse about potential legal consequences after the researcher publicly disclosed six zero-day exploits and posted proof-of-concept exploit code. The disclosure has drawn scrutiny from cybersecurity experts, including researcher Kevin Beaumont, who questioned Microsoft's response approach.

The incident highlights a longstanding tension in cybersecurity: researchers must balance protecting users through vulnerability disclosure against the industry practice of privately coordinating with vendors to allow time for fixes before public release. The researcher expressed concern about Microsoft's threats, citing potential severe personal consequences.

cards.headline: GitHub Copilot switches to token-based billing model
cards.teaser: Microsoft's GitHub introduced a new token-based billing system for Copilot, replacing the previous pricing structure.
cards.body:
GitHub changed its billing approach for Copilot, the AI-powered coding assistant, moving to a token-based payment model. The shift has prompted negative reactions from some developers who use the service.

The previous version of GitHub Copilot offered a different pricing structure that some users found more predictable. Token-based billing measures usage by the amount of AI processing required rather than a flat subscription fee, which can lead to variable monthly costs depending on how much a developer uses the tool.

cards.headline: Google's Gemini Spark AI assistant launches for Ultra subscribers
cards.teaser: Google released Gemini Spark, an AI assistant designed to automate everyday tasks, to users with Ultra subscriptions in the United States.
cards.body:
Google's Gemini Spark AI assistant is now available to Ultra subscribers in the United States. The tool automates everyday tasks like summarizing inboxes and planning local events, operating as a dedicated product separate from Google's other AI services.

According to early reviews, Gemini Spark proves useful for managing routine activities with continuous support throughout the day. The decision to launch it as a standalone product rather than integrating it into existing Google services has drawn attention from tech observers.

cards.headline: Former Snap employees launch Ghost Angels investment fund
cards.teaser: Twenty alumni from Snap formed a new investment fund focused on supporting emerging social media companies.
cards.body:
Twenty Snap alumni have joined together to create Ghost Angels, an investment fund focused on backing emerging social media startups. The fund leverages the collective experience of its founders, who built and operated one of the major social platforms.

This effort reflects a broader pattern among veteran tech employees who are establishing investment funds to support new companies in their fields of expertise. Social media continues to attract venture capital investment as an active sector.

cards.headline: Meta developing AI-powered wearable pendant
cards.teaser: Meta is working on an AI pendant device as part of its hardware product lineup.
cards.body:
Meta is building an AI-powered pendant device, expanding its portfolio of hardware products beyond virtual reality headsets and smart glasses. The pendant would represent another effort by the company to integrate artificial intelligence into wearable form factors.

Meta has invested heavily in AI-powered hardware as part of its broader technology strategy. The company already sells Ray-Ban smart glasses with AI features and continues to develop virtual and augmented reality devices.

cards.headline: Nintendo releases compatibility updates for original Switch games on Switch 2
cards.teaser: Nintendo issued a new batch of software fixes to improve how original Switch games run on the Switch 2 console.
cards.body:
Nintendo released additional backwards compatibility fixes for games originally designed for the Switch console to run on the Switch 2. The update addresses issues with older titles running on the newer hardware.

Backwards compatibility allows owners of the newer console to play games from the previous generation. Nintendo has been releasing periodic updates to improve performance and fix bugs that occur when running older software on the Switch 2.

When the deadlock could not be broken through regulation and extra time, the match went to penalties. Eberechi Eze missed for Arsenal in the second round after a stuttering run, though David Raya kept his side alive by denying Nuno Mendes in the third round.

Gabriel stepped up for the decisive kick knowing he had to score to keep Arsenal's hopes alive. He was briefly delayed by referee Daniel Siebert as nerves mounted. The defender opted for power but blazed his attempt over the crossbar, sparking celebrations from the PSG fans behind the goal as red flares lit up the stadium.

The defeat marks a painful conclusion to what had otherwise been a historic season for Arsenal. The club won their first Premier League title in 22 years earlier in May, ending a drought that began after their Invincibles campaign in 2004. An open bus parade to celebrate the domestic triumph was scheduled for the following day, creating a bittersweet end to their campaign.

For PSG, the victory confirms their status as Europe's dominant force. Becoming back-to-back Champions League winners underscores their position among the continent's elite clubs.

The final was shaped by contrasting approaches, with Arsenal defending aggressively while PSG sought to impose their attacking patterns. Arsenal's young midfielder Myles Lewis-Skelly impressed throughout, while Gabriel proved to be a commanding presence at the back before his penalty heartbreak.

The shootout loss denied Arsenal the chance to complete a domestic and European double, a feat that would have cemented their status among the greatest modern teams. Instead, they must reflect on narrowly falling short in the competition's showpiece event.

cards.headline: Scotland midfielder Billy Gilmour ruled out of World Cup with knee injury
cards.teaser: Billy Gilmour will miss the World Cup after suffering a knee injury during Scotland's friendly win over Curacao.
cards.body:
Scotland midfielder Billy Gilmour has been ruled out of the World Cup after sustaining a knee injury during Saturday's 4-1 friendly victory over Curaçao.

Despite the positive result, which saw Scotland's performance improve significantly after Curaçao were reduced to 10 men, the injury to Gilmour cast a shadow over the win. The news emerged later on Saturday night. Manchester United's Fletcher has been mentioned as a potential replacement for the Scotland squad ahead of the tournament.

cards.headline: Defending champion Coco Gauff eliminated from French Open in third round
cards.teaser: Coco Gauff's title defense ended with a third-round loss to Anastasia Potapova at the French Open.
cards.body:
No. 28 seed Anastasia Potapova pulled off a stunning upset, defeating defending champion Coco Gauff 4-6, 7-6 (1), 6-4 in the third round of the French Open. Potapova recovered from losing the first set to claim victory in a tightly contested match.

The fourth-seeded American struggled in crucial moments, particularly in the final set where she held a break lead at 3-all but failed to convert several break points. Gauff acknowledged her inability to capitalize on key opportunities under pressure as her bid to retain the title came to an end.

cards.headline: Darren Till knocks out Aaron Chalmers in first-round BKFC debut
cards.teaser: Darren Till won his bare-knuckle boxing debut with a brutal one-punch knockout of Aaron Chalmers after surviving an early knockdown.
cards.body:
Darren Till demolished Aaron Chalmers with a one-punch knockout in his Bare Knuckle Fighting Championship debut at BKFC 90 in Birmingham. Till secured the stoppage victory after recovering from being knocked down earlier in the fight.

The former UFC fighter's transition to bare-knuckle boxing proved successful despite the early scare. The event also featured an interim title fight between Connor Tierney and Rico Franco.

cards.headline: Vegas Golden Knights announce ticket sales for Stanley Cup Final against Carolina
cards.teaser: The Golden Knights released on-sale details for the Stanley Cup Final as they prepare to host the Hurricanes.
cards.body:
The Vegas Golden Knights announced ticket sale details for the Stanley Cup Final against the Carolina Hurricanes, with games hosted at T-Mobile Arena. The team plans to hold an official watch party at the venue for away games.

The Hurricanes reached their first Stanley Cup Final in 20 years after breaking through their Eastern Conference final roadblock. Under coach Rod Brind'Amour, Carolina finally ended years of playoff heartbreak to earn the chance to compete for the championship.

cards.headline: Tennessee softball defeats Texas Tech with walk-off home run at Women's College World Series
cards.teaser: Tennessee advanced in the Women's College World Series with a walk-off home run victory over Texas Tech.
cards.body:
Tennessee softball won its opening round game at the Women's College World Series against Texas Tech, clinching the victory with a walk-off home run. The seventh-seeded Volunteers defeated the 11th-seeded Red Raiders in the 1-0 game.

Tennessee advances in the tournament after stifling the Texas Tech offense throughout the contest.

cards.headline: British boxer Adam Azim stops Steve Claggett in third round in London
cards.teaser: Adam Azim continued his march toward a world title shot with a third-round stoppage of Steve Claggett.
cards.body:
British light-welterweight Adam Azim secured a third-round stoppage victory over Steve Claggett in London. The win keeps Azim on track for a potential world title opportunity.

The stoppage victory demonstrated Azim's credentials as a rising contender in the division. The fight took place in front of a London crowd.

hero.headline: Italy Cancels Ye and Travis Scott Concerts Over Security Concerns
hero.body:
Italian authorities canceled scheduled concerts by rappers Ye and Travis Scott over security concerns, according to reports. The concerts were set to take place in Italy but were banned by local officials.

The cancellations came after officials raised public order and safety issues related to the planned performances. Both artists had scheduled appearances in the country as part of their touring schedules.

The decision to ban the concerts was made by Italian authorities who cited security concerns as the primary reason for the cancellations. The specific nature of the security threats or concerns was not detailed in the available reports.

Ye, formerly known as Kanye West, has faced controversy in recent years that has led to canceled performances and dropped partnerships. Travis Scott has also faced scrutiny following a crowd crush incident at his Astroworld festival in 2021 that resulted in multiple deaths.

The Italian concert ban affects performances that were scheduled to take place in at least one Italian city. The decision represents a significant disruption to both artists' European touring plans.

Neither Ye nor Travis Scott had publicly commented on the cancellations at the time of the reports. The artists' representatives also had not issued statements regarding the Italian authorities' decision.

The concert ban joins a series of venue and performance cancellations both artists have faced in various locations. Italy's decision to cancel the shows on security grounds marks the latest challenge to their ability to perform in certain markets.

Local authorities in Italy have the power to ban public events they deem to pose security or public order risks. The cancellations came after an assessment of potential safety and security issues related to the planned concerts.

Fans who purchased tickets to the canceled shows will need to seek refunds through their point of purchase. No alternative dates or venues in Italy were announced as part of the cancellation notices.

cards.headline: Trump to Open Great American State Fair After Music Acts Cancel
cards.teaser: President Trump will headline the opening of a Great American State Fair after several musicians canceled their scheduled performances.
cards.body:
President Trump announced he will kick off the Great American State Fair after multiple music acts withdrew from the event. The fair is part of celebrations for a 250th anniversary.

Several performers canceled their scheduled appearances at the fair, prompting organizers to bring in Trump as the headline act. Vanilla Ice, one of the few musicians who did not cancel, defended his decision to perform at the event, telling critics that music has no political rules.

cards.headline: Morgan Wallen Flips Piano During Denver Concert After Technical Issue
cards.teaser: Country singer Morgan Wallen flipped a piano on stage after experiencing a technical glitch during a performance of Sand In My Boots at a concert in Denver.
cards.body:
Morgan Wallen physically flipped a piano during his Denver concert after equipment failed mid-performance. The incident occurred while Wallen was performing his song Sand In My Boots.

Video footage captured Wallen's reaction to the technical issue, showing the singer overturning the piano on stage. The outburst came after the equipment malfunction disrupted his performance during the concert.

cards.headline: Niall Horan Reflects on Former Bandmate Liam Payne's Death
cards.teaser: Niall Horan spoke publicly about the death of his former One Direction bandmate Liam Payne, who died in 2024 at age 31.
cards.body:
Niall Horan opened up about the death of Liam Payne in an interview with The Times of London. Payne died in 2024 at age 31 after falling three floors from a hotel in Buenos Aires, Argentina.

Horan said he was with Payne in Argentina shortly before his death. Describing his feelings about the loss, Horan said there is sadness, but it also makes him laugh and smirk because of the memories the two shared during their time together in One Direction.

cards.headline: Tom Holland Expresses Interest in Mentoring Next Spider-Man Actor
cards.teaser: Tom Holland told Empire magazine he looks forward to helping whoever takes over the Spider-Man franchise, similar to how Robert Downey Jr. mentored him.
cards.body:
Tom Holland recently told Empire magazine that he's eager to help establish the next actor who will take on the Spider-Man role. He expressed enthusiasm about supporting the transition and potentially playing a mentoring role similar to what Robert Downey Jr. provided when Holland first joined the Marvel franchise as Peter Parker.

Holland indicated openness to the successor being Miles Morales or another Spider-Man variant character, emphasizing his willingness to guide whoever steps into the role next.

cards.headline: Hannah Waddingham Denies Auditioning for Wicked Role
cards.teaser: Hannah Waddingham confirmed she never auditioned for the role of Madame Morrible in Wicked, shutting down speculation about a failed audition.
cards.body:
Hannah Waddingham addressed claims that she auditioned for the role of Madame Morrible in the film adaptation of Wicked. The Ted Lasso star confirmed she never auditioned for the part.

Waddingham's statement shut down speculation that had circulated about a failed audition attempt for the musical film. The actress directly denied the claims, clarifying that she was never in consideration for the Madame Morrible role.

cards.headline: Pete Davidson Praises Ex-Girlfriend Kim Kardashian on Podcast
cards.teaser: Pete Davidson called Kim Kardashian superhuman and praised her acting abilities during an appearance on a podcast with Nikki Glaser.
cards.body:
Pete Davidson spoke positively about his ex-girlfriend Kim Kardashian during a podcast interview with Nikki Glaser. The comedian described Kardashian as superhuman and complimented her skills as an actor.

Davidson told the podcast that Kardashian is so good at acting. The comments came after Davidson's recent split from Elsie Hewitt, with the comedian choosing to praise his former relationship with the reality television star and businesswoman.

hero.headline: U.S. military disables ship attempting to breach Iranian port blockade
hero.body:
The U.S. military prevented another vessel from reaching an Iranian port on Friday, continuing its enforcement of a naval blockade in the Strait of Hormuz. U.S. Central Command announced the action against a ship flying under a Gambian flag after it ignored repeated warnings from American forces.

The disabled vessel represents another instance of the military taking direct action as part of the broader blockade that has closed Iranian ports to commercial shipping. Central Command did not provide specific details about how the ship was disabled, the condition of the vessel, or the status of its crew.

The Strait of Hormuz, a narrow waterway between Iran and the Arabian Peninsula, represents a critical route for global oil shipments. The U.S. blockade has created significant shipping disruptions in recent weeks by preventing vessels from entering Iranian ports.

This enforcement action comes as Washington and Tehran work toward a potential agreement that could reopen the Strait of Hormuz and extend a current ceasefire. Diplomatic sources have indicated that reopening the strait constitutes a key element of any deal between the two governments. That agreement was announced this week and now awaits approval from President Trump and Iranian officials.

The timing of the military intervention adds complexity to ongoing negotiations between the two nations. The blockade and related diplomatic efforts follow months of escalating tensions between the United States and Iran over regional security and economic matters.

Central Command has not disclosed the total number of vessels that have encountered the blockade. This marks at least the second publicly known instance of direct military action against a ship attempting to breach the blockade, though the military has not revealed how many ships complied with warnings and turned away before facing intervention.

The blockade represents part of a broader U.S. strategy to apply pressure on Iran while simultaneously pursuing diplomatic talks. The delicate balance between military enforcement and negotiation efforts highlights the complexity of the current situation in the region.

U.S. officials have characterized the blockade as necessary for regional security and to support negotiations. However, the enforcement action demonstrates the military dimension of American policy toward Iran, even as diplomats work to reach a settlement.

The outcome of the negotiations could significantly reshape the strategic landscape in the Middle East. If successful, the agreement would remove restrictions on Iranian shipping and represent a major shift in U.S. policy toward Tehran.

The incident also reflects broader maritime tensions in the region, where multiple actors maintain competing interests and capabilities. The Strait of Hormuz has long served as a flashpoint for geopolitical competition, and the current blockade underscores its continued strategic importance.

cards.headline: Lead prosecutor withdraws from Comey criminal case
cards.teaser: The federal prosecutor who secured an indictment against former FBI Director James Comey has stepped down from the case.
cards.body:
The federal prosecutor who obtained an indictment against former FBI Director James Comey has withdrawn from the case, according to a court filing submitted Friday. A notice of substitution filed in the Eastern District of North Carolina confirmed the change in legal representation.

Comey faces criminal charges for allegedly threatening President Trump's life in a social media post featuring seashells that has since been deleted. The filing did not provide a reason for the prosecutor's departure from the case.

cards.headline: Federal judge to review Trump's $1.8 billion anti-weaponization fund
cards.teaser: A judge has agreed to review a $1.8 billion fund announced by President Trump earlier this month.
cards.body:
A federal judge has agreed to review President Trump's $1.8 billion anti-weaponization fund following a third-party motion challenging the settlement. The motion claims the fund "is a product of collusion and is itself a fraud on the court."

Judge Kathleen Williams reopened Trump's $10 billion lawsuit against the Internal Revenue Service, which stemmed from the leak of the president's and his sons' personal and business tax returns by a former contractor. The fund has drawn broad criticism since its announcement, creating divisions within the Republican Party.

cards.headline: New Jersey governor and DHS secretary coordinate response to protests at immigration facility
cards.teaser: Governor Mikie Sherrill deployed state police to a Newark immigration detention center facing escalating protests.
cards.body:
Protests outside the Delaney Hall immigration detention center in Newark, New Jersey continued into their ninth day on Saturday, with detainees engaged in a hunger and labor strike demanding improved conditions and medical care.

State police deployed barricades to separate demonstrators supporting the detained immigrants from a group of Trump-supporting counterprotesters who gathered outside the facility. The competing groups faced off across the police barriers, with both sides chanting slogans and displaying signs reflecting their opposing positions on immigration enforcement.

cards.headline: Senate candidate's wife told campaign about his messages to other women
cards.teaser: The wife of Maine Senate candidate Graham Platner alerted campaign staff that he exchanged sexually explicit messages with other women.
cards.body:
Amy Gertner, wife of Maine Democratic Senate candidate Graham Platner, told former senior campaign staffer Genevieve McDonald about sexually explicit messages her husband had exchanged with other women, according to reports from The New York Times and The Wall Street Journal. The disclosure to campaign staff occurred last year.

The reports provide new information about Platner's conduct during his campaign for the U.S. Senate seat. Both publications independently confirmed that Gertner had informed campaign personnel about the messages.

cards.headline: Security preparations underway for America 250 celebrations in Washington
cards.teaser: Washington prepares for events marking the nation's 250th anniversary amid concerns about political violence.
cards.body:
Security operations have begun across Washington ahead of multiple events commemorating America's 250th anniversary this summer. The preparations follow recent incidents including a shooting outside the White House complex.

The first scheduled event, a UFC fight at the White House, will take place in the coming weeks. That event comes two months after the shooting incident near the complex.

cards.headline: White House denies report about chief of staff advising Vance on social media
cards.teaser: The White House rejected a New York Times report claiming chief of staff Susie Wiles suggested Vice President Vance take a break from social media.
cards.body:
The White House denied a New York Times report that alleged chief of staff Susie Wiles recommended Vice President Vance step back from social media use. White House Communications Director Steven Cheung called the report complete fake news.

Cheung responded on social media platform X, writing that the Times story was not true. The denial came shortly after the newspaper published its account of the alleged advice from Wiles to the vice president.
